 -versus-

entities.text: High Court Of Orissa At Cuttack
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Opposite Party(s)

Mr. B. K. Ragada, Aga
 Mr. S. K. Behera, Advocate for O.P.2
 Coram: Justice Sibo Sankar Mishra

Order
13.09.2024 Order No.
03. 1. Heard.

2. At the instance of opposite party No.2, the F.I.R. dated 08.02.2024 in Tumudibandh P.S. Case No.26 of 2024 for the offences under Sections 376(2)(n)/376(2)(I)/313 of I.P.C. came to be registered against the petitioner.
At the stage of investigation, the parties have settled their dispute.

3. The allegation against the petitioner is that on 08.02.2024, the opposite party No.2 being the complainant/informant lodged an F.I.R. alleging therein that the petitioner had been keeping physical relationship with her since last 3 years with false promise of married.
It is alleged that due to such relationship, she became pregnant and subsequently on the instigation of the petitioner, she terminated her pregnancy.
It is also alleged that the petitioner is now avoiding her.

Hence, the F.I.R.
4.
The petitioner and the opposite party No.2 are present in the Court and being represented and identified by their respective counsels.
They have also filed self-attested copies of their Aadhaar Cards to establish their identity, which are taken on record.

5. The opposite party No.2, who is 24 years of age, has filed an affidavit dated 02.09.2024 inter alia stating as under:-
<3.

That, in the meantime on the intervention of our family members as well as the village gentries, the dispute between us giving rise to lodging of the above F.I.R. has been amicably settled and the matter has been compromised between myself and the petitioner.

sentences.text:
That, in the above circumstances and the present development of the case, I do not want to proceed further against the petitioner in the aforesaid criminal proceeding.=
6.
On query from the Court, the opposite party No.2/victim has stated that there are proposals for her marriage.
Due to pendency of the present case, her prospective of marriage is getting affected.
Therefore, she does not want to proceed with the case against the petitioner rather prefers to put a quitous to the entire dispute.
Although this aspect of the matter has not been mentioned in the affidavit, however, she has stated the same orally.

7. Mr. Ragada, learned Additional Government Advocate for the State submits that since the parties have settled their dispute and present in the Court, there is no legal impediment in quashing the F.I R.
8.

Regard being had to the fact that the parties have settled their dispute and keeping in view the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and another reported in 2012 (10) SCC 303 and B.S. Joshi & others vs. State of Haryana & another reported in (2003) 4 SCC 675

sentences.text: , I am of the considered view that subjecting the petitioner to trial would be a futile exercise.
Therefore, the petition deserves merit.

9. Accordingly, the criminal proceeding in C.T. Case No.29 of 2024 arising out of Tumudibandha P.S. Case No.26 of 2024 pending in the Court of the learned J.M.F.C., Tumudibandha and the consequential proceedings arising therefrom qua the petitioner are quashed, subject to the petitioner paying a cost of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees ten thousand) to the victim/opposite party No.2.
109.
The CRLMC is accordingly disposed of.
